item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=formal+models+of+research+agenda+abandonment+in+science+and+autonomous+discovery&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6820898\", \"title\": [\"Formal Guarantees for Trustworthy Autonomous Biological Discovery: A Dual-Process Control Framework\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Generative AI now proposes protein sequences and metabolic pathways faster than laboratories can validate them, yet autonomous biological discovery is stalled by an unaddressed trust deficit: in-silico predictions regularly diverge from in-vitro outcomes, and no formal framework exists to bound this gap. We introduce Verifiable Agentic Biotechnology (VAB), a theoretical framework built on three provable guarantees. First, conformal prediction converts point estimates of biological fitness into finite-sample confidence intervals, guaranteeing coverage of true physical fitness with probability at least 1α irrespective of model misspecification. Second, a dual-process Constrained Markov Decision Process routes designs between fast heuristics and expensive mechanistic verifiers, achieving exact computational savings (C 2-C 1)P(σ 1 ≤ τ) while bounding safety degradation at γP(σ 1 ≤ τ). Third, the in-silico to in-vitro reproducibility gap is formalized as a Wasserstein distribution shift, yielding a Distributionally Robust Optimization bound V * DRBO on wet-lab transferability. Each bound is validated on controlled proxy environments and, in the case of conformal prediction, on real protein sequence data. The framework's parameters-α, τ , and ρ-map directly onto regulatory variables, providing a path from ungoverned sequence generation to auditable biological design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6820898\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1002/9783527855841.ch14\", \"title\": [\"Materials Agents for Autonomous Research\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/9783527855841.ch14\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 3, 17]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6797083\", \"title\": [\"Employment Latency: A Formal Framework for Autonomous Employment Infrastructure, Discovery Latency Resolution, and Point-of-Offer Compliance Integration\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This…
